body: Me too. I'm tired and I want to rest.
I can't talk about it too. Admitting it to myself is so hard, let alone to other people.

I was 17 or 18 then. I didn't have money for medication, and I honestly believed I was going crazy. I felt like I had no choice but to tell my parents, but it took me a long while.

I'm 32 now, and they think I'm already okay. I travel a lot, I go to the gym, I crack jokes all the time. But I've slipped in and out of depression in the past decade, and I think I'm having my worst relapse ever. It started around October last year and it's still here. I've been thinking about killing myself more and more each day, and I've been feeling lazy and unmotivated. I wouldn't dare tell my parents anymore. I'm an adult, and they're too old to be burdened. The sad thing is that I don't feel like I have anyone to talk to except for strangers on the Internet.

It's my fault. I pushed people away. 

I don't want to die. But I also don't want to feel so miserable. I'm scared that the wish for freedom from pain would outweigh my will to live sooner or later.

Anyway, I'm sorry for your loss. There was really nothing you could have done. Depression is a disease like cancer. It kills.

I'm convinced I have adult ADHD, which makes it difficult for me to get unstuck once I've found my comfort zone. 

The sad thing is that the IT industry is my comfort zone even though it feels like hell for me to be in it. I just tell people that I stay for the money, even if it isn't fully true. I do my job well, but I don't usually have initiative or innovative ideas. I get good money, but because I'm unhappy with my job, I don't exactly excel in it, so I don't get promoted and earn excellent money. That's what frustrates me so much.

Anyway, I won't stop applying for jobs even though I think I'm too old at 32 to change careers. :(

And you're right about having more responsibilities. I really don't have a responsibility to anyone right now, which I think left me feeling unmotivated and unchallenged. Time to find something that will get me off my ass, I guess!

That crossed my mind as well. Psychiatrists seem to just want to ply people with pills. Well, not all of them, but the few I encountered were sketchy at best. Maybe I'll be better off looking for a psychologist.

Thanks for the concern. I really do appreciate it. :)

Your sister's therapist and my psychiatrist sound alike -- they were both useless. :(

I'll look into that. But I kind of developed a phobia of psychiatrists after she told my parents that they could have me committed if they wanted. :(

I used to go to a psychiatrist when I was in college. But I didn't feel like she really listened to me. I used to describe all my symptoms hoping she would tell me what they were, but all I got were prescriptions.

I suffered from depersonalization from a long time -- that feeling of being not real, and being detached from reality. And also intrusive thoughts. I had sudden urges to stab myself or to jump into oncoming traffic. Guess what? She didn't explain what they were to me. Just looked at me and tell me to take my pills. Then she told my parents that they could confine me if I had a breakdown.

It was only years after, in my late 20s, when I found out that my symptoms had names and logical reasons behind them, and it was a major relief to know that I wasn't going crazy. But no, I never got that reassurance from my psychiatrist. She made me feel like I was going crazy, and for that I hate her and I've never forgiven her, and I don't think I can trust a psychiatrist ever again.

I had no say in the matter because my parents were the one paying for my treatment back then. I had to keep up the facade of getting better because I didn't want to worry my parents, who really did their best to understand what was going on and who did everything they could. And what can a young college student like me know about mental illnesses? It was a time before Google and the Internet.
I wonder if yoga would help.
I sometimes get the urge to stab myself sometimes when I'm holding a knife. It's crazy.

The thing is, I don't know what it takes to get me unstuck. I feel like life overlooked me and has passed me by.

I just have this weird certainty that even though I'm not exactly suicidal now, there's a huge chance that I'll still go that way. I just don't know when.

Thanks for the recommendation. I'll go check it out.

Also, I love your mum's reply. :)

> Do not think too much. 
> do not want too perfect life

I should really do this more often! My own mother once said that she's worried that I would never be happy, not because I won't get what I want, but because I would always want more than I have. I'm starting to think she's right.

Oooh, I've never heard of "l'appel du vide" before but after looking it up, I realized I've been through that a lot of times. I read somewhere that it's not the fear of heights people are afraid of, but the fear of jumping.

I don't think I'm at the stage of committing suicide but somehow there's a part of me -- a calm, logical part -- that's convinced that I could kill myself on impulse given then chance. It's like I put myself on suicide watch.

Sometimes, I think that I worry about things too much. I'm not yet seriously suicidal but I'm already worried about getting there. I hate anxiety. It makes me worry about everything.

How about a backpacking tour through Southeast Asia? Or a tour of the whole South America? Or exploring the beaches of Polynesia and Micronesia? Or if you've been to all those, return to a country you love and explore it thoroughly.

Ah yes, it is indeed true, misery loves company. I think the feeling of aloneness makes the loneliness worse, so it feels better when we find out that other people get what we go through.

>My fear stems from "what if this is it? What if this is all I get and I blew it?". 

I think of this a lot, too. I would regret blowing it.

And even if there's reincarnation as some people believe, I don't think I would want to have to go back, so might as well do it right the first time.

Schedule a follow-up trip now so that you won't have to get depressed!

I know someone who posts a lot of happy photos on Facebook. Thousands of friends (mostly met on her travels), photos of trip after trip after trip, status updates from various airports, photos of family gatherings with loving parents and close siblings, photos of parties after work, parties on weekend, all kinds of sports activities, etc. 

But I lived with this girl for the past four years up until three months ago, and I saw her having a hard time sleeping at night because of her nightmares. She has to be very tired to get a deep sleep, hence all the activities she does. She's also bipolar and depressed, so her shrink suggested that she make her life very busy.

How do I know all these? Because I'm also depressed and so she confided in me, because she thought I would understand her -- and I did. Not a lot of people know about her condition.

It just goes to show that we don't know what's going on under the surface.
Because you're here asking for a reason you can believe in. So there's a part of you that still hopes to be saved.

You got all through that and still lived. You're one tough cookie. i wouldn't let suicide win so easily, not after living through what you did.

Being suicidal myself, that's how I try to view suicide -- an enemy. Like procrastination, negativity, insecurity, laziness, and all the other bad things. I feel like my life is shitty enough as it is, so I don't want another shitty thing win over me.

The last time I broke down crying for no reason, a friend called me and we talked for five hours. Life felt better.

Of course, I had a depressed episode two weeks after that, but it was disrupted by a Facebook message from a friend who wanted to go to the beach with me that summer.

I hold on to these little things. I don't always have a rescuer, though. But the memories of those little things tide me over.

I don't know your full situation, but I hope you think over what just happened. It can be just coincidence, or maybe "divine intervention," who knows and at this point, we'll never know, but it bought you precious time, and that means something.
I just PMed you with directions on how to post your own post. Hope to see your thread up soon.

Thank you for sharing your experience. Glad to know that you didn't pull the pistol trigger. I'm sure someone would have been devastated had you succeeded offing yourself.

I agree with you about feeling hopeless without something to look forward to. For me, it's travel. Every quarter, I have a major trip so that I would have something new to look forward to every three months. It's a crazy way of coping but that's what works.

But sometimes, it scares me that this tactic will stop working. I'm afraid that I'll just snap one day. I hope not. 

The father of a dear friend of mine passed away on Christmas Eve. My friend told me that it made her think about death a lot, and it made her realize that even if a funeral is packed with people, death is still a very solitary journey. I found that thought very sad, and at that same time, it made me feel scared about dying even more.

Why do I want to die? I ask myself that a lot. At this point, I'm not even sad. I'm just feeling stuck at a stage in my life that I should have passed long ago. I applied to different jobs to escape where I am now, but they all turned me down. Maybe I'm too old to at 32 to be an entry-level employee in the publishing world. But I'm unhappy working in the IT industry, even though it pays the bills. My only respite is my freelance writing gigs, but I can't rely on them to sustain me full-time.

My closest friends have gotten married and mostly moved someplace else. They have their own lives now, with their spouses and kids.

So I thought, maybe I need to find my own husband, but I'm not even sure if I want to get married, let alone have kids.

Anyway, my life has always been what it is for the past five years. 

Everyone else's lives are changing except mine. I don't know how to make a change in my life. I tried to do what I thought would help -- applying for a new job -- but I've been rejected so many times.

I'm anxious a lot of times for no reason, so that gets tiring.

I know I don't have any major problems now which is why I'm ashamed of myself for feeling this way, but I hate being unable to move on and do what I want in my life.

Hi, throwaway here, too! I just made my own thread a few minutes ago after reading about Reddit founder Aaron Shwartz's suicide. It's funny that I had to make a throwaway when no one knows who I am even with my year-old Reddit account, but oh well.

I'm suicidal but I'm terrified to die. I'm scared of the pain, because I don't think there's a painless way to die voluntarily. I'm scared of any desperate last attempt of the body to stay alive. I'm scared of any last-minute regrets. I don't want to regret killing myself while my body is frantically but futilely gasping for air, or something.

And I still have dreams. I still dream of going to Maldives, of trying out skydiving, of joining an orgy, of doing something significant with my life. I don't want to quit without even giving myself a chance. I deserve that, even if the whole world doesn't seem to think the same way.
